en.title: SPC Flooring Subfloor Flatness: Buyer Checklist | Luvie
en.heading: SPC flooring subfloor flatness: what to check before ordering
en.description: Separate flatness from moisture and level. Build a site acceptance record before ordering SPC flooring for renovation or distribution projects.
en.lead: A flooring order can match the approved colour and still arrive at a site that is not ready for installation. For a distributor supplying a renovation in Brazil or a commercial interior in Uzbekistan, the missing detail may be the substrate rather than the plank. This guide is about documenting floor geometry before purchase. It complements moisture checks; it does not replace them or supply a universal installation tolerance.
en.answer: Ask for the exact flooring model's installation instructions, a measured substrate survey and a written preparation plan. A floor that looks level in a photograph is not necessarily flat enough for the selected system. Do not use extra underlay as an assumed repair for unevenness.
sections: Flat, level and dry are different acceptance questions

Level describes the relationship to horizontal. Flatness describes local departures from a plane. Dryness is a separate condition requiring the specified test method. A surface can satisfy one and fail another. Before asking an installer to approve the room, identify the current substrate, previous coverings, repairs and any changes in height at doorways. Request the relevant instructions for the exact SPC construction and locking system, including permitted substrate types and underlay. Tarkett's linked guide illustrates why substrate condition is important for its own flooring collection; its values must not be transferred to a different SPC product. Keep the manufacturer's instructions and the project specification together so an attractive sample does not become the only purchase criterion.
Create a usable survey, not one reassuring photograph

Ask the site professional to record the survey method, measuring tool, locations, date and observed deviations. Mark high spots, depressions, changes between rooms and previously patched areas on a simple floor plan. Measurements should be compared with the current model-specific requirement, not a tolerance copied from a search result. Include door clearances and transitions to adjacent finishes because preparation can change finished floor height. Photographs should show where observations were taken, rather than merely showing a straightedge somewhere in the room. If the site team has not inspected the base, label the survey as pending and make that uncertainty visible to the buyer. This is a practical handoff record, not a claim that one visual inspection is a complete installation assessment.
Assign preparation before scheduling the delivery

A commercial quotation should distinguish the flooring supply from substrate preparation. Ask who will assess repairs, specify compatible preparation materials and accept the completed surface. Do not assume a thicker plank or a softer underlay makes an uneven substrate acceptable. Check whether the selected floor has attached underlay and whether an additional layer is permitted at all. Where existing flooring will be removed, the final preparation scope may remain provisional until the substrate is exposed. Agree when it will be reassessed and who can change the programme. For a multi-room order, a single approved room does not automatically release every other room. Keep preparation, moisture acceptance and delivery storage as separate checkpoints to avoid treating a delivered pallet as approval to begin installation.
Put the acceptance evidence into the purchase handoff

Record the model, plank construction, installation-guide revision, substrate description, measurement record, preparation responsibility and acceptance date. A sample approval confirms what was actually reviewed; it does not prove that every site condition is suitable. If the project changes the underlay, substrate or installation method, send the revised combination back for assessment. Buyers often ask whether they can quote flooring before the survey: an indicative supply quote can be discussed, but site suitability should remain explicitly unresolved. Ask the installer for a room-by-room release rather than a generic statement that the floor is fine. Store these records with the order so the importer, local distributor and installation team are working from the same conditions instead of conflicting messages.
en.closing: Send the intended room use, substrate type, measured survey and selected flooring reference with your inquiry. Use the catalog to shortlist finishes, then request the current installation documentation for the exact model.

sourceName: Palram PVC care guide — applies to the named Palram products, not Luvie approval

en.title: PVC Wall Panels and Disinfectants: What to Check | Luvie
en.heading: Can a cleaning chemical damage a decorative PVC wall panel?
en.description: Check the exact decorative finish, cleaner and cleaning method before specifying PVC wall panels for hospitality, retail or managed interiors.
en.lead: The purchasing team approves a wood-look sample, but the facilities team already uses a different cleaning chemical throughout the building. That mismatch is easy to overlook in a hotel refurbishment or retail rollout. Choosing decorative PVC wall panels requires a discussion about the finished surface and the cleaning routine, not simply a statement that PVC is easy to wipe. This is a procurement compatibility checklist, not a disinfectant recipe or a hygiene certification.
en.answer: Compatibility depends on the exact panel surface, chemical formulation and method of use. Obtain model-specific written care instructions and agreement on the proposed routine before ordering. Do not transfer another manufacturer's approved-cleaner list to a decorative Luvie finish.
sections: Identify the layer that the cloth will touch

The material name does not describe every surface treatment. Ask whether the chosen model has a printed layer, film, coating or textured face, and request the maintenance instructions for that construction. Keep the finish reference and sample batch identifiable. A cleaner tolerated by one plain PVC sheet is not automatically suitable for another decorated surface or its joint sealant. Palram's published guide warns about chemical and abrasive damage and recommends checking cleaners on an inconspicuous area for its listed products. That supports asking compatibility questions; it does not certify a Luvie panel or authorise the same chemicals. Procurement should obtain a specific answer instead of converting a general statement about plastic into a building-wide cleaning policy.
Give the supplier a complete cleaning brief

Obtain the cleaner's exact commercial name and current technical information from the facilities team. Record the intended dilution, contact time, application method, wiping material, frequency and any rinse requirement as specified by the cleaner's manufacturer. Do not improvise a stronger concentration or mix products. Include the parts around the panel: trims, sealants and adjacent finishes may have different instructions. Ask the panel supplier which parts of this routine have supporting information and which remain unverified. Keep cleaning and disinfection objectives distinct; a visually clean wall is not proof of a particular hygiene outcome. For regulated environments, the relevant project specialists must define the required system and evidence rather than relying on a decorative product page.
Agree a controlled sample review before a full rollout

Where the suppliers approve a trial, use an identified sample of the exact finish and retain an untreated comparison sample. Document the agreed method and inspect the appearance under consistent light after the prescribed process. Record dulling, colour change, surface tackiness or other visible changes without assuming that no visible change proves long-term compatibility. A sample trial is a screening step, not a laboratory durability test or a guarantee for repeated service. If the cleaning routine is mandatory and evidence is unavailable, leave the finish unapproved rather than hiding the uncertainty. A hotel corridor and a back-of-house service space may need different material choices even when a purchasing team wants one colour palette throughout.
Hand over a maintenance record with the order

Keep the approved finish, written care instructions, cleaner identification and review outcome together. Give the installer and facilities team the same record; a maintenance note that never reaches the cleaning contractor cannot protect the selection process. Define who reviews substitutions when a cleaner is changed after opening. Buyers sometimes ask whether every disinfectant is safe on PVC: there is no blanket answer for all decorated panels. Others ask whether an inconspicuous test is enough: it may reveal an immediate appearance problem, but it is not evidence for every exposure or service life. Ask for the narrowest supported claim and preserve any exclusions. This makes the handover useful without inventing performance that the selected product has not demonstrated.
en.closing: Share the finish reference and the proposed cleaner documentation when requesting samples. Start with the catalog for appearance, but approve the maintenance routine separately before placing a project order.

sourceName: Australian Department of Agriculture: ISPM 15 export FAQ — confirm destination rules separately

en.title: Wall Panel Wood Packaging: ISPM 15 Buyer Checks | Luvie
en.heading: What should wall panel importers check about wood packaging?
en.description: Separate the panel material from pallets, crates and dunnage. Ask the right wood-packaging questions before approving an international shipment.
en.lead: A wall panel may be plastic-based while its pallet, crate or loose blocking is made from timber. The product description therefore does not answer the wood-packaging question. Importers buying for South America, the Gulf or Uzbekistan should resolve the actual packing construction with their supplier and destination adviser before shipment. This guide helps prepare that discussion; it is not a country-specific customs ruling or a promise that a particular consignment will be accepted.
en.answer: Check every packaging component, not just the panels or the crate face. Identify raw timber, processed-wood parts and loose dunnage, then ask the destination's plant-protection authority or qualified import adviser which current requirements apply. Do not assume that calling a crate plywood resolves a mixed-material package.
sections: Separate the product from the packing materials

Request a packing-material list alongside the product and carton specifications. Include pallets, skids, framing, cross-battens, internal blocks and loose supports. Photographs should show the assembled package and its construction, not only a wrapped exterior that conceals the base. The Australian agriculture authority's FAQ distinguishes raw-wood packaging from packaging made wholly of qualifying processed wood, and notes that requirements depend on importing countries. This is useful background, not a substitute for checking the destination. Do not infer treatment status from the panel's material or a supplier's generic export experience. A product order and its packing arrangement are separate things that both need clear descriptions.
Review mixed materials and any later substitutions

A plywood-sided crate can still include raw timber in its base or framework. Ask the packer to identify such components before approving the arrangement. If a forwarder adds support timber during consolidation, that addition also belongs in the review. Avoid approving only a drawing while allowing any locally available substitute at packing time. Instead, record the approved material construction and require notification of a change. Ask your destination adviser how to handle the actual mix and which evidence is needed. Do not treat the source FAQ's exemptions as universal permission for every shipment, or apply a mark yourself. Treatment and marking must follow the applicable authorised system, and the responsible provider should be identifiable.
Request evidence at a useful point in the shipment

Agree when photographs and packing details will be available for review, ideally before the finished units become inaccessible. Ask for clear images of applicable marks where required, their location on the package and the package identification to which they relate. A blurred photograph or a generic certificate detached from the actual packing is difficult to reconcile with the shipment. Send the evidence to the appointed import adviser or broker for the destination rather than asking a sales representative to guarantee customs acceptance. Also record the final package count and any changes after inspection. These are practical traceability requests; they do not establish that photographs alone meet the destination's documentary or inspection requirements.
Keep phytosanitary checks separate from transport protection

Wood-packaging compliance does not by itself demonstrate that panels are protected against bending, corner damage, water entry or shifting. Review mechanical protection and transport handling as a separate packing discussion. Likewise, strong wrapping does not settle plant-health requirements. Put two distinct acceptance lines into the order handoff: destination-related packaging review, and suitability of the agreed protective packing for the product and route. If a crate or pallet is repaired, reused or replaced, ask whether that changes the previous acceptance. Before dispatch, reconcile the approved construction, final photographs and shipment identifiers. Unresolved destination requirements should be raised before cargo moves rather than being concealed behind a broad export-ready label.
en.closing: Send your destination, intended transport route and packing constraints with the product inquiry. Confirm current packaging requirements through the relevant destination authority or import professional before approving dispatch.
